content.text: {"id":"b7fc665c-5454-4f76-aa07-c1cc4c8a5a9f","audio_id":"b73fe357-f2c5-4e08-a16e-489e7b438547","status":"complete","created_at":"2026-11-16T05:01:39Z","answer":"The track keeps the bright, sweet feminine nursery-pop character: the lead is clearly sung with a tuneful, bouncing contour and natural phrase shapes, not a hard-processed word drill. At about 114 BPM (4/4), the bass and clipped rhythm-guitar-like accents keep a light bounce while the claps mark the groove. Korean diction is mostly clear; both 고양이 and 강아지 are sung as complete words in the audible refrains. The verse-to-hook transitions feel natural. Some short call-and-response bits are brisk, but I don’t hear them as genuinely chopped or unnaturally rushed. The vocal begins around 0:02. There is a short instrumental passage around 0:51–0:53 and another brief gap near 0:59–1:00; vocals continue afterward. The last lyric begins around 1:12 and the ending sounds like it reaches the final phrase, though the transcription/alignment only catches it through “놀,” so its text timing is uncertain. A longer instrumental tail follows, continuing to about 1:28. The apparent scattered or truncated lyric entries in the alignment are not, by themselves, evidence that words were cut off in the audio."}
